_comment: Physical parameters for tools/gen_rhodes.py. ALL VALUES ARE PRIORS (ESTIMATE) until the reference fit (IMPLEMENTATION-v3 §7) replaces them.

t60_v1._doc: sustain T60 of V1 (s) at MIDI keys, log-interpolated; flat below the first point, halving every 10 keys above the last (floor). Source: Shear 2011 tine Q (1974 Mark I), T60 = 6.908 Q/(pi f0) (research/09)

tinebar._doc: bar_cents_points: [midi, cents of the bar's own f0 relative to the tine] (Muenster & Pfeifle ISMA 2014 Table 1, research/09); k_rel coupling rel. to w_t^2 (ESTIMATE); mu bar/tine mass (ESTIMATE); tine T60 = target; bar T60 multiple (ESTIMATE)

release_t60._doc: damper-on T60 (s) by MIDI upper bound (soft targets, jRhodes sfz)

strike._doc: strike point from the clamp (m) at key 21 and key 108, linear in key (R05 W1)

bands._doc: hammer tip bands: first MIDI key of each band (A0 = position 1 of R05 W1)
bands._doc_tip: hammer tips per band (Rhodes service manual ch. 4, R05 W1/W2): Shore A durometer of the neoprene (null = maple wrapped in shrink tube) and tip size (inch). The Hertz contact stiffness follows from them (gen_rhodes.band_K).

hammer._doc: Hammer = a rigid mass at the tip on a Hertz rubber tip, F = K e^1.5 (1 + alpha de/dt) (Hunt-Crossley), against the tine's first 6 FE modes. Effective mass = min(mass_kg, m_tine1 / m_eff_ratio) (gen_rhodes.hammer_mass): 11 g (R02 Tab. 3.2) in the bass, where the contact then lasts ~5.7 ms at v = 100 (Muenster & Pfeifle 2014 measured 6.42 ms on average), down to ~0.5 g in the treble, where a heavier hammer followed the tine and re-struck it 2..12 times (the FM-1 scan's 23 dB holes). alpha: neoprene loss (s/m, ESTIMATE). E_wrap: the wood band's wrapped-maple face (Pa, ESTIMATE). v_max, range_db: hammer speed at v = 127 and its range (dB) down to v = 1.

tip_peak_gap_v127._doc: V1 tip peak (gap units) at v = 127: bass .. treble

pickup._doc: pole radius / gap per family (R03 code geometry: R = 1 gap); family 0 = 1/16 inch gap, family 1 = 1/32 inch gap. R = 2 gave a non-monotonic velocity response (2026-10-15 test), so both start at 1.0 until the fit.

types._doc: Physical voicing per TYPE, relative to the STAGE 77 priors. off: pickup offset change in gap units (+ = toward the pole axis: H2 up, fundamental down, 'bell'; - = off-axis: round, mellow; W6). bark: tip displacement / gap scale (pickup distance: closer = more bark and output, W3); the gain is compensated by 1/bark. ham: hammer contact-rate scale (felt tips 1970-71 are softer: longer contact, fewer high partials; W2/W9). bell: tine overtone (O1/O2) force scale. rlc: pickup inductance x cable/input capacitance resonance [f_hz, q]. body: up to 2 biquads after the load: [kind, f_hz, q, gain_db], kinds hp2 / peak / lshelf / hshelf; the amp and speaker of the instrument (Suitcase: Peterson preamp into four 12-inch speakers, W5/W6; Dyno-My-Piano: active treble-boost preamp). level_db: output trim so the types play at matched loudness (measured A3 v100 + A4 v70, host).

_doc_levels: gain_target_dbfs: RMS (50..300 ms) of one voice at v = 100, every key exactly; set so a 4-note chord at v = 127 peaks near -3 dBFS (host, effects bypassed). peak_dbfs: a global cap on 90 % of the keys single-voice v = 127 peaks (+3 dB); it does not bind at this target.

velocity_trim._doc: small per-key RH_PAMP trim at the velocity anchors so each key's level curve (re v = 104) follows the median curve of all keys (monotonic). The physics (hammer_contact) is already even to ~3 dB; the trim is bounded to +-max_db and reported in rhodes_spec.json (pulse.pamp vs pulse.pamp_phys). iterations 0 = physics only.

voicing._doc: pickup voicing: H2/H1 (dB, 30..300 ms) of a v = 100 strike per key; each key's tip scale (b) is set to it (gen_rhodes.voice_pickups). A Rhodes at mf is mostly fundamental (R05 W3: the bass voiced for 'mostly fundamental'; W6 E3: fundamental loudest); the bark grows with the tip swing toward v = 127. Replaces tip_peak_gap_v127 as the b scale (that one only sets the starting point).
